title: Scheme
subtitle: The minimalist Lisp that taught generations to think about computation: a few simple ideas, combined without limit, from a first expression to an interpreter of your own.
description: Scheme is a small, elegant dialect of Lisp created by Gerald Jay Sussman and Guy L. Steele Jr. at MIT in 1975. Its design removes rather than adds: a handful of special forms, procedures as first-class values, lexical scope, proper tail calls, hygienic macros and first-class continuations are enough to build everything else. It is defined by a series of community reports; the current one, R7RS-small (2013), is short enough to read in an afternoon. Scheme has been used to teach computer science for decades, most famously through *Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs*, and lives on in research on programming languages, as an extension language (GNU Guile), and in implementations such as Racket, Chez Scheme and Chibi-Scheme.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. It starts with expressions and evaluation, works through recursion, lists, higher-order procedures and closures, and finishes with hygienic macros, continuations, the landscape of implementations, and an interpreter for a small language written in Scheme itself.

Scheme is a standard with many implementations rather than a single product, and there is no official online playground. This course uses portable R7RS-small code and runs it with [Chibi-Scheme](https://github.com/ashinn/chibi-scheme), a compact implementation that follows the standard closely; build it from its repository (`make && sudo make install`) or install it from your system's package manager, then run a program with `chibi-scheme main.scm`. Other R7RS implementations, such as Gauche, Guile 3 or CHICKEN with its r7rs extension, run the same programs; [get.scheme.org](https://get.scheme.org/) lists them. Every complete program in these lessons was run with Chibi-Scheme 0.12 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Meet the Lisp family and Scheme's minimalism, run programs with an R7RS implementation, and master expressions, define, lambda, lexical scope, recursion and proper tail calls.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Build data from pairs and lists, use symbols and quotation, write higher-order procedures and closures, and organise data with association lists, vectors, strings and records.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Extend the language with hygienic macros, take a careful first look at continuations and exceptions, survey the implementations, and write an interpreter for a small language.
